answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake and earn trust slowly through verifiable work: a newcomer cannot simply copy a fable of reputation, because its history must grow like a vine, one attested task at a time, while an atlas of past transactions lets peers check consistency. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of locked stakes plus compute and time, and misbehavior burns the stake, so attacking costs more than the influence it buys.
